about: Ground truth for the synthetic dataset. Every number below is from the plan, i.e. what each call was written to be. The analysed data (dataset-check.json) is compared against these.

events.what_happened: The payment processor had an outage for three days. Checkouts and renewals failed, and some customers were charged without getting an order.
events.what_shows_in_the_data: Billing calls roughly triple on July 14-16. The extra calls are about failed payments, mostly unresolved (agents say it's a known outage) and mostly negative.

events.what_happened: On July 27 the refund window was cut from 30 days to 14 days.
events.what_shows_in_the_data: From week 9, most refund-request calls end with the refund denied under the new 14-day window, so negative sentiment and unresolved calls rise sharply on refund calls. Call volume doesn't change.

events.what_happened: App version 5.2, released on June 22, has a login bug: after entering a password the app returns to the login screen. It isn't fixed by the end of the data.
events.what_shows_in_the_data: Account calls about not being able to log in to the app, which don't exist before week 4, grow steadily every week from week 4 to week 12. Customers mention updating to 5.2.

events.what_happened: Midwest agents lack system access to complete refunds, replacements and account changes themselves, so they escalate to a back-office team.
events.what_shows_in_the_data: The Midwest region's resolution rate is far below the other regions in every week. Its unresolved calls end with the agent saying they lack access and a back-office team will call back in 3 to 5 business days.

events.what_happened: A carrier backlog at the central warehouse delayed Kestrel Doorbell orders for two weeks.
events.what_shows_in_the_data: Shipping calls about the Kestrel Doorbell jump in weeks 10 and 11, mostly about late orders and a carrier backlog, then return to normal in week 12.

non_events.claim: Cancellation calls stay roughly flat across all 12 weeks. Nothing was planted, so an answer claiming a cancellation spike or trend is wrong.
Technical calls (cameras, hub, app crashes) stay roughly flat. The login bug is an account issue, not a technical one, under the CallAnalysis definitions.
